title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory Explained
text:
Cognitive dissonance, a key concept in social psychology, describes the mental discomfort experienced by a person who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values. This state of inconsistency motivates individuals to reduce the psychological stress by changing one of the conflicting cognitions or introducing new ones that rationalize the behavior.

The magnitude of dissonance is proportional to the importance of the involved cognitions. For example, if an individual spends significant money on a product they later realize is faulty, they are motivated to change their perception of the item (e.g., focusing only on its positive features) rather than accept the inconsistency between their spending and the item's poor quality.
